newsitem.title: CHINA: China tells Manila not to disrupt Spratly peace.
newsitem.headline: China tells Manila not to disrupt Spratly peace.

text.p: Beijing on Thursday urged Manila not to disrupt peace and stability in the disputed Spratly Islands after the Philippine navy destroyed Chinese structures there.
"(This) is another serious encroachment upon China's sovereignty," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Tang Guoqiang told a news briefing.

"We hope the Philippine side... will not do things that are not beneficial to the healthy development of bilateral relations and not do things that are not beneficial to peace and stability in the region," he said.
The Philippines said this week it had destroyed new structures it believes China built near areas claimed by Manila in the Spratlys.
The Spratlys are a cluster of islands, reefs and atolls in the South China Sea believed to sit atop huge oil and gas reserves and which Beijing says historically belongs to China.
The area is also claimed totally or in part by Vietnam, Taiwan, Malaysia and Brunei as well as the Philippines.
In 1995, the Philippines removed or destroyed several markers or floating buoys, which Manila said the Chinese set up at six reefs and shoals near the islands it claims in the Spratlys.
China-Philippines relations have been strained by competing claims over the islands.

In April, Manila accused Beijing of sending naval vessels near two islands occupied by Filipinos. Beijing in turn accused Manila of violating China's sovereignty after Filipinos flew their flag over a cluster of rocks called Scarborough Shoal north of the Spratlys.
Last month the Philippines arrested 21 Chinese fishermen near Scarborough and charged them with illegal entry after rejecting China's demand for their release.
